title: Authorization equivalence over engine task tables (VI.4 + A-3)
database: PostgreSQL 17 (Testcontainers postgres:17-alpine), one database per engine

scenarios.name: Random policies: SQL list == {t : allow(t)} == in-memory model, count equal, for 3 seeds x 8 principals (0..300 groups)
No post-filtering: LIMIT/OFFSET pages of the predicate query are full and their concatenation equals the full list
Explicit deny wins (A-3): over a broader grant, over a user-level grant, a broader deny over a specific grant; conditional rows fail closed; a deny of another permission does not hide
Tenant binding: grant rows of another tenant never leak; a request tenant id only filters inside the allowed set
Revocation: a new deny (policy_version bump) applies to the very next list and object check (no cache)
Q2: the same predicate through the engine's own native task query API returns the same list and count, without engine patches
p95 list latency with a 300-group principal (plain SQL and engine native query), reduced scale; pass criterion p95 < 200 ms

scenarios.name: Q2 probe: what the engine's own TaskQuery / authorization offers for this filter

measurements.engineAuthorizationService: none: Flowable 8.0.0 has no authorization service or permission tables (no ACT_RU_AUTHORIZATION); access is modelled only as identity links (ACT_RU_IDENTITYLINK: candidate user/group, assignee, owner)
measurements.taskQueryOptions: taskCandidateUser / taskCandidateGroup(In) / taskInvolvedUser / taskTenantId: OR of identity links, no deny, no wildcard resource, no permission bits, no extension hook for an extra SQL clause
measurements.nativeTaskQuery: yes: TaskService.createNativeTaskQuery() accepts raw SQL with #{named} parameters and returns Task entities and counts (used in E2-6/E2-7); no engine patch
measurements.whatItWouldNeed: keep the product predicate: a product query builder over ACT_RU_TASK (plain SQL or NativeTaskQuery) plus the same for ACT_HI_* history tables; or a custom MyBatis mapper. Either way the engine's TaskQuery API cannot be the read path for protected lists (VI.4 rule 3)

notes.scale: REDUCED: 2000 engine tasks (target in XI.4: 10,000) x 300 groups; 4 tenants with skew 45/25/20/10 %
notes.table: ACT_RU_TASK (engine-owned), columns TENANT_ID_ and ID_; predicate from AuthorizationPolicy.visible

scenarios.name: Q2 probe: what the engine's own TaskQuery / authorization offers for this filter

measurements.engineAuthorizationService: yes: AuthorizationService + ACT_RU_AUTHORIZATION (GRANT / REVOKE / GLOBAL), applied to TaskQuery when authorizationEnabled and an authentication is set
measurements.productRuleExpects: x hidden in A, B and C (any matching deny wins, compiled as NOT EXISTS)
measurements.a3Reading: A and B are inside A-3's wording (deny vs a grant at the same or broader scope). C (a broader deny vs a narrower grant) is outside the wording but inside the compiled NOT EXISTS rule; Operaton lets the narrower grant win
measurements.taskQueryOptions: candidate user/group(In), tenantIdIn, OR-queries; no hook for an extra SQL clause
measurements.nativeTaskQuery: yes: TaskService.createNativeTaskQuery() with raw SQL and #{named} parameters (used in E2-6/E2-7); no engine patch; native queries are not checked by the engine's authorization
measurements.whatItWouldNeed: built-in authorization would need deny precedence over user-level grants and over grants in other groups (A-3), the product's permission bits/conditions and tenant binding; otherwise keep it off (as the adapter does) and use the product predicate through plain SQL or NativeTaskQuery

notes.scale: REDUCED: 2000 engine tasks (target in XI.4: 10,000) x 300 groups; 4 tenants with skew 45/25/20/10 %
notes.table: ACT_RU_TASK (engine-owned), columns TENANT_ID_ and ID_; predicate from AuthorizationPolicy.visible

scenarios.name: Q2 probe: what the engine's own TaskQuery / authorization offers for this filter

measurements.engineAuthorizationService: yes: AuthorizationService + ACT_RU_AUTHORIZATION (GRANT / REVOKE / GLOBAL), applied to TaskQuery when authorizationEnabled and an authentication is set
measurements.productRuleExpects: x hidden in A, B and C (any matching deny wins, compiled as NOT EXISTS)
measurements.a3Reading: A and B are inside A-3's wording (deny vs a grant at the same or broader scope). C (a broader deny vs a narrower grant) is outside the wording but inside the compiled NOT EXISTS rule; Operaton lets the narrower grant win
measurements.taskQueryOptions: candidate user/group(In), tenantIdIn, OR-queries; no hook for an extra SQL clause
measurements.nativeTaskQuery: yes: TaskService.createNativeTaskQuery() with raw SQL and #{named} parameters (used in E2-6/E2-7); no engine patch; native queries are not checked by the engine's authorization
measurements.whatItWouldNeed: built-in authorization would need deny precedence over user-level grants and over grants in other groups (A-3), the product's permission bits/conditions and tenant binding; otherwise keep it off (as the adapter does) and use the product predicate through plain SQL or NativeTaskQuery
